question_type: geometric (CAGR) annual rate of change of a ratio of two columns of one table between two month-end rows two years apart, decimal to thousandths
decisive_step: Take the ratio as Balance > Working balance over Balance > Total (not over Current assets > Total) from the General Fund composition table, at the calendar month-end rows Dec 1938 and Dec 1940 (not the FY rows), and annualise over n=2 with a geometric (root) formula. Reference: worklog.md Step 0 (ambiguity resolved: 'total balance' = Balance > Total because working + seigniorage + increment sums to it), evidence treasury_bulletin_1939_01.txt:496 (Dec 1938 row) and treasury_bulletin_1941_01.txt:815 (Dec 1940 row), vintage check Step 4 (every reprint identical; no later revision of Dec 1938).

notes: Useful for v10 tooling. (1) The same table is titled four different ways across issues ('Composition of Treasury General Fund' 1939_01-04, 'Composition of General Fund' 1939_05-1940_12, 'Composition of the General Fund' 1941_01-02, 'Balance in the General Fund of the Treasury' 1941_03 on, with columns reordered from 1941_03) and has no printed id; printings matched by title tokens across the renames (a[14] found the 1941_03+ family for Dec 1940; c[19] found 1941_01/02 under the older title) but find_tables shows them as separate groups, which sent b and c to the 1940_12 issue first even though Dec 1940 is only in 1941+ issues. A 'first issue printing period P' hint in find_tables ('rows 1933..Nov' already implies it, but the model did not use it) or a printings-first workflow for month-end rows would save the paging in c[13]-c[16]. (2) The 1939-40 Composition table's column labels are OCR-garbled ('Seign-lorage', 'Deposite in Fed. Reserve Banke') and the 1940_01 printing has 'Current assets > Inactive gold' and 'Current liabilities' mislabelled relative to other issues (b[16] header); the two columns used were labelled correctly in every printing, so no harm, but a column-order check across printings would catch a shift. (3) The row_coverage rule bound the Dec 1938 row's unused cells (seigniorage, increment on gold, current-asset components) as if the model had summed a partial row; the rule needs the compute op, not just the cell count.
